cases.customer_question: What should be done when no stored ICS is found and profile testing is performed using manually selected PTS options?
question_variants: Can PTS testing be performed without imported ICS?
Should testing proceed when ICS cannot be located?
cases.actual_issue: Testing proceeded using manually selected profile options because the expected ICS was not found. The tester assumed the ICS was unavailable and did not escalate the issue, resulting in a test configuration that differed from the intended qualification configuration.
cases.plain_english_explanation: The tester could not find the expected Bluetooth configuration file and manually selected settings instead. Later it became clear that the correct configuration should have been verified and matched to the qualification project. The manual setup contributed to inconsistent results.
cases.consultant_answer: When an expected ICS cannot be located, the issue should be escalated and resolved before relying on manual configuration. Qualification evidence must be traceable to the intended design configuration. Using manually selected options can produce a different effective ICS and invalidate comparisons with customer qualification results.
cases.decision_logic: Qualification testing depends on the accuracy of the ICS definition. If the authoritative ICS is unknown or unverified, test execution may not represent the qualified design.
cases.final_recommendation: Stop and verify the authoritative ICS source, compare it against Qualification Workspace data or exported project ICS information, then rerun testing using the verified configuration.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Testing may be performed against the wrong feature set, producing misleading failures, unnecessary retesting, incorrect customer guidance, and qualification confusion.
